content: A maculopapular rash is characterized by a flat, red area on the skin that is interspersed with small, raised bumps. By definition, it includes both macules, which are flat, discolored areas of the skin, and papules, which are small, raised lumps. This type of rash may resemble the appearance of spots or pimples, similar to those seen in measles. Maculopapular rashes are commonly observed in patients with conditions such as scarlet fever. Additionally, this type of rash can occur as a side effect of consuming large doses of niacin or no-flush niacin, typically in the range of 2000 to 2500 mg, which is sometimes used therapeutically to manage low levels of HDL cholesterol.
